result:
I added `GET /api/operations/recent`, which only administrators can call. It returns one page of operations dated within the last 30 days. I didn't run the build or any tests, so none of this has been compiled or exercised.

- **Endpoint:** `getRecentOperations` in `OperationResource` takes a `Pageable` and sends the usual pagination headers. `@PreAuthorize` restricts it to the admin authority. The literal `/recent` path takes precedence over `/{id}`.
- **Service:** the new `OperationService` has a read-only `findRecent` method. It computes the window from an injected `Clock` (30 days ago up to now), as the backend rules require.
- **Repository:** I added `findByDateBetween(Instant, Instant, Pageable)` to `OperationRepository`.
- **DTO:** the endpoint returns a new `OperationDTO` record (id, date, description, amount, bankAccountId), so entities don't leave the service layer. Labels are not included.
- **Clock bean:** the project had no `Clock` bean, so I added `ClockConfiguration` in `config`, which provides `Clock.systemUTC()`.

I marked the new resource method with a comment saying it is hand-written, as `docs/architecture.md` asks.

I put the endpoint on the `/api/operations/recent` path you asked for. `docs/api.md` says admin-only resources normally live under `/api/admin`, and it prefers query parameters for filtering. The admin restriction is enforced by `@PreAuthorize` instead.
